sentences.text: ..... Respondents  JUDGMENT

This is a petition filed u/s. 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, claiming for compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.

2. The petitioner's case in brief as follows:
On 21-12-2021 at about 8.15 p.m. when the petitioner was proceeding on the motor bike bearing No.KA-04-JB-8419 as a pillion rider, at that time, driver of the car bearing No.KL-73-C-2747 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and MVC NO.156/2022 3 JUDGMENT dashed against the petitioner, as a result of which he fell down and sustained injuries.
Immediately petitioner was taken to Prolife multispeciality hospital wherein he was treated as inpatient for 4 days and discharged from the hospital and still under treatment.
Petitioner spent amount for treatment, conveyance, nourishment etc.,
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.10 lakhs from the respondents.
3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.2 remained exparte.

The respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel before the Tribunal and filed written statement wherein contended that they issued the policy in respect of the car bearing No.KL-73-C-2747, but the original copy of the policy is in the possession and control of the respondent No.1.
The person driving the vehicle has no relation in force as on the date of accident to drive the vehicle.
The driver of the insured vehicle has no valid and effective driving licence to drive the car at the time of accident.
MVC NO.156/2022 4 JUDGMENT
This respondent seeks protection under section 147 and 149 of MV Act.
Further contended that second respondent has violated the Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

The owner and insurer of the motor cycle are also necessary and proper parties to the case,
without impleading the said parties the case is not maintainable.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant and without any basis.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

4. From the above said pleadings my predecessor in office has framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing reg.No.KL-73-C-2747 on 21-12-2021 at about 8.15 p.m. at B.B.Main road,
near coffee day, Yelahanka, Bengaluru city ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?
From whom?

2 3. What Order or Award?
MVC NO.156/2022 5 JUDGMENT 5.
The petitioner examined himself as P.W1 and examined two witnesses as PW.2 and PW-3 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.22 documents.
The respondents have not lead either oral or documentary evidence.

6. Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
7.

My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1: In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Ex-P1 to Ex-P13 documents as wound certificate, adhar card, medical bills, inpatient bill, salary slips,
FIR, wound certificate, spot mahazar, rough sketch, IMV report, col133 MV Act Notice, reply notice, charge sheet.
9.

The evidence and materials on record reveals MVC NO.156/2022 6 JUDGMENT that soon after the accident one Manjunath have filed complaint before the jurisdictional police on the basis of which Yalahanka traffic police registered the FIR against the driver of the car bearing reg.No.KL-73-C- 2747.

Thereafter the jurisdictional police filed through and detailed investigation and filed the charge sheet against the driver of the car as per Ex-P13 by holding on 21-12-2021 at about 8.15 p.m.
in the Bangalore- Ballari main road near coffee day accused drove the Hondai car bearing reg.No.KL-73-C-2747 in high speed, rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life from Devanahalli towards Hebbal and hit to the back side of the Bazaz platina motor cycle bearing No.KA-04-JB-8419 driven by the Richerd along with the Manjunath as a pillion rider.

10. Apart from this on perusal of the Ex-P3 spot mahazar and Ex-P4 sketch, it clearly shows that the spot of accident was a two way highway road and the accident has been taken place on the left side of the MVC NO.156/2022 7 JUDGMENT road.

Further Ex-P4 clearly demonstrate that the rider of the motor cycle was proceeding on the left side of the road and at that time, the driver of the offending vehicle car came from the back side and hit to the back of the motor cycle.
Moreover as seen from Ex-P4 there was sufficient space on the right side of the offending vehicle to move on the road.

Thus Ex-P4 clearly shows that accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent Richard.A vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62538325/
3 driving of the offending vehicle.

entities.text: Richard.A vs New India Ass Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Moreover the respondent has not examined the driver of the offending vehicle to disprove the evidence of the PW-1.
11.

On perusal of the cross-examination counsel for the respondent though filed the objections contending that the accident has been taken place due to the self accident and not due to the first respondent car, but has not examined the driver of the offending car or any of the eye witness.

Even in the cross- examination of PW-1 except by putting the single MVC NO.156/2022 8 JUDGMENT suggestion that the accident has not been taken place due to the negligence of the driver of the car nothing else was elicited from the mouth of the PW-1 with regard to the non involvement of the car.

On perusal of the cross-examination of the PW-1 respondent counsel has not at all denied the involvement of the car in the accident at least by putting the single suggestion.
12.
The respondent No.2 has not lead any rebuttal evidence and disprove the evidence of the PW-1.
Even there is no materials and evidence placed on record to prove that the charge sheet and the police documents are collusive and effective.

13. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a MVC NO.156/2022 9 JUDGMENT particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
14. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Though the respondents have denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove their defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.

15. In addenda, in a claim for compensation MVC NO.156/2022 10 JUDGMENT U/Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS.
ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

sentences.text:
With this observation issue No.1 in is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
16. ISSUE NO.2:
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

sentences.text: AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 34 years.

The petitioner has produced the Ex-P.10- aadhaar card which reveals petitioner's year of birth is 1988 and as on the date of accident,
he was 33 years.

The petitioner has stated that he was working at MVC NO.156/2022 11 JUDGMENT cargo village, International Airport, Devanahalli and earning Rs.27,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and deformity.
The petitioner has produced Ex-P11-salary slips.
Ex-P12-statement of account.

On perusal of Ex-P12,
which reveals petitioner was drawing the salary of Rs.34,685/-p.m. as on November 2021 i.e., as on the date of accident.
Respondent has not disputed this document.

Thus the income of the petitioner as on the date of accident was Rs.34,685/- p.m.
18.
LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:-
In this case, PW-1 himself clearly admitted that during October 2024 he was getting salary of Rs.54,000/-.
Thus it is clear that due to the injuries sustained in the accident, petitioner has not lost his job and lost his future income.

19. Though petitioner has examined the doctor as MVC NO.156/2022 12 JUDGMENT PW-3 who has deposed in his affidavit that petitioner has sustained permanent disability from upper limb and wholebody at 15%, but as petitioner himself in his cross examination admitted that during October 2024 he was getting salary of Rs.54,000/-, it clearly shows that petitioner has continued the job and drawing the more salary than he was drawing the salary as on the date of accident.
Thus it is clear that petitioner has not sustained functional disability.

20. Relying upon the ratio laid down in ILR 2010 KAR 2439 (Subhash V/s The New India Assurance Co.Ltd)-
Claimant continued in service after accident.

ILR 2010 KAR 2439 (Subhash V/s The New India Assurance Co.Ltd)-
Claimant
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Award of compensation towards loss of future income by the tribunal-legality of Held-If the claimant is continued in service then question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise.
21. Therefore it is clear that the claimant does MVC NO.156/2022 13 JUDGMENT not have any functional disability.
Unless the actual financial loss arising out of physical disability is made out, a claimant is not entitled for compensation towards loss of future income due to disability.

22. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained (1)CLW present over the scalp, left front parietal region (2) abrasion present over both hands, swelling present over left wrist (3) left shoulder dislocation with fracture base of 5th metacarpal of left hand 4) multiple abrasions over the face limbs and the doctor has opined that the above said injuries are grievous in nature. PW-3 further stated that petitioner sustained injuries i.e., left shoulder anterior dislocation, non union fracture left scaphoid, CLW frontoparieal scalp, multiple abrasion and petitioner underwent Richard.A vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62538325/
5 surgery in the form of closed reduction and conservative management for scaphoid fracture in Prolife hospital.
MVC NO.156/2022 14 JUDGMENT 23.
The petitioner has stated that he is suffering with permanent disablement and deformity to attend his work and to do daily activities.
Hence petitioner is suffering from whole physical and mental pain and agony and injuries sustained by him.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner being 33 years, certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.75,000/- under this head.

24. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
PW-1 in his cross examination admitted that due to the injuries sustained in the accident he has taken the leave of 3 months and he has not received the salary during that period and sustained loss of pay for 3 months.
Hence, petitioner has sustained loss of pay for only 3 months.
Hence he is entitle for the loss of pay for 3 months.

25. By considering the nature of injuries MVC NO.156/2022 15 JUDGMENT sustained by petitioner and conservative treatment taken by him in the Prolife hospital, Bangalore, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 3 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.1,04,055/- (34,685 X 3) under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
26. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is a resident of Rayapuram, Chamarajpet, Bangalore and sustained injuries i.e., (1)CLW present over the scalp, left front parietal region (2) abrasion present over both hands, swelling present over left wrist (3) left shoulder dislocation with fracture base of 5th metacarpal of left hand 4) multiple abrasions over the face limbs and the doctor has opined that the above said injuries are grievous in nature and petitioner was inpatient in the hospital for MVC NO.156/2022 16 JUDGMENT 4 days and underwent surgery in the form of closed reduction and conservative management for scaphoid fracture at Prolife hospital, Bangalore and certainly he would have hired the cab for traveling to the hospital and certainly, it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of his treatment the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.

Hence a sum of Rs.10,000/-
under this head.

sentences.text: 6 27. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The petitioner being the owner cum driver by profession, certainly injuries sustained by him will cause the disability.
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.

Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment &
frustration and MVC NO.156/2022 17 JUDGMENT also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.
28. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
With regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner has produced Ex-P14-medical bills for Rs.5,035/- and Ex-P4-inpatient bill for Rs.1,05,865/-.

The said Ex-P4 inpatient bill for Rs.1,05,865/-, in that petitioner has paid Rs.12,100/-
and Star health and allied insurance paid Rs.93,765/-.

The petitioner in his cross-examination admitted that he had claimed insurance from his office, but the entire medical bill has not been reimbursed and he has paid only Rs.30,000/- from his hand towards the medical expenses.

Hence this tribunal is awarding Rs.30,000/-
towards medical expenses.

29. The calculation table stands as follows :
1

Attendant charges, extra : 10,000/-
 nutritious food &
 conveyance charges  MVC NO.156/2022 18 JUDGMENT 2 Pain & sufferings : 75,000/-
3 Loss of income during laid- : 1,04,055/-
 up period 4 Loss of future amenities & : 25,000/-
 happiness 5

Medical expenses : 30,000/-
 Total 2,44,055/-
Hence the petitioner is entitle for compensation of Rs.2,44,055/-.
30. INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

sentences.text: There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.1 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of MVC NO.156/2022 19 JUDGMENT claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
32. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
-: O R D E R :-
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.2,44,055/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
After deposit of the compensation  MVC NO.156/2022 20 JUDGMENT amount to the petitioner,entire amount shall be released to him through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
32. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
-: O R D E R :-
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.2,44,055/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
After deposit of the compensation  MVC NO.156/2022 20 JUDGMENT amount to the petitioner,entire amount shall be released to him through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
